function.name: make_webapi_call
function.description: Executes a call to a specified Web API endpoint with given parameters and returns the response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

endpoint.description: The URL of the Web API endpoint to be called.

method.description: The HTTP method to be used for the API call.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested or submitted.

params.description: Query parameters to be appended to the endpoint URL.

query.description: The search term for the query.

body.description: The JSON payload to be sent with POST, PUT, or PATCH requests.

data.description: The actual data to be sent in the request body.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for a server response before timing out. This is a float type value.

Here’s a quick guide to hunting down a three‑bedroom flat (or maisonette) in Zürich: | What you’ll need | Where to look | |------------------|---------------| | **Budget** – Typical rent for a 3 BR in central zones (e.g., Kreis 1–5) starts around CHF 2 500/month and climbs steeply into the high‑four figures if you’re after luxury or prime locations. In outer districts (Kreis 10+), prices drop to roughly CHF 1 800–2 200.
**Preferred district(s)** – e.g., Seefeld, Enge, Oerlikon, Zollikon, Wipkingen, Langstrasse, Uetliberg.
**Move‑in window** – Some landlords require a deposit + first month’s rent upfront; others accept lease agreements signed within weeks.| • **Homegate.ch** – Switzerland’s largest portal; filter by “Wohnung” → “Zimmer”, set max/min rooms, price range, location.
• **ImmoScout24.ch** – Similar filters plus map view & neighbourhood stats.
• **Newhome.ch / Newcity.ch** – Good for newer developments and apartments under construction.
• **Zürcher Immobilien AG** – Local agency specializing in Zürich rentals.
• **Facebook Marketplace & Groups** – “Zurich Apartments/Rooms” groups often list off‑market deals. | ### How to narrow your search 1. **Set clear criteria:** - Minimum square footage (~90 m²). - Desired amenities (balcony, parking, elevator, furnished/unfurnished). 2. **Use advanced filters:** - On Homegate/ImmoScout, choose “Mietwohnung” → “Mehr als 2 Zimmer”. - Add “Balkon/Terrasse” or “Parkplatz” as needed. 3. **Check neighborhood statistics:** - Look at average rental rates per m² via local reports or the Swiss Federal Statistical Office. 4. **Schedule visits early:** - Popular areas get booked quickly—try weekend afternoons when many owners open their doors. 5. **Prepare documents:** - Salary slips, employment contract, credit report (“Schufa”), reference letters from previous landlord. - Many landlords will also ask for a guarantor if your income isn’t sufficient relative to the rent (rule of thumb ~3× monthly net salary). ### Budget example | District | Avg. Rent (CHF/m²) | Approx. Monthly Rent (3 BR, 100 m²) | |----------|--------------------|-------------------------------------| | Central (Kreis 1–5) | 35–45 | 3 500–4 000 | | Suburban (Oerlikon, Zollikon) | 25–32 | 2 500–3 200 | | Outer (Langstrasse, Uetliberg) | 20–28 | 2 000–2 600 | *(Prices fluctuate seasonally.)* --- #### Next steps * Pick one or two target districts based on commute time, lifestyle, and budget. * Create accounts on Homegate and ImmoScout, save your preferences, and enable email alerts so new listings hit your inbox instantly. * If you’d like more personalized assistance, consider contacting a local agent who specializes in multi‑family units—they can sometimes access exclusive listings before they appear online. Let me know which districts interest you most or what your budget looks like, and I can tailor further suggestions!
